obligations.expected_behavior: Before evaluation, create a candidate-external trust envelope that freezes validator content identity, complete semantic-dependency identities, support policy, and scope; invalidate the envelope when any member is missing, ambiguous, or changed.
forbidden_result: Evaluation relies on a candidate-controlled or incomplete trust envelope.
A missing, ambiguous, or changed trust-envelope member is accepted as valid.
obligations.observable_result: A pre-evaluation trust envelope contains the required frozen bindings and deterministically invalidates on missing, ambiguous, or changed members.
obligations.state_after: Validator trust is bound by a valid candidate-external envelope or rejected as invalid.
obligations.state_before: Validator trust has not been established through a complete frozen pre-evaluation envelope.
obligations.subject: Validator trust envelope

obligations.expected_behavior: Define semantic-dependency closure to include every executable, data, policy, configuration, and environment representation that can affect target selection, verdict, diagnostic category, or evidence validity, without narrowing the closure by Probe reachability.
forbidden_result: Any affecting dependency category is omitted from the closure.
Probe reachability is used to narrow the semantic-dependency closure.
obligations.observable_result: The closure definition enumerates all five required categories and records that Probe reachability cannot reduce it.
obligations.state_after: An exhaustive, non-narrowed semantic-dependency closure is defined for the replay result.
obligations.state_before: The replay dependency closure lacks an independently verified exhaustive category and reachability rule.
obligations.subject: Semantic-dependency closure
obligations.trigger: Replay dependencies are enumerated or verified.

obligations.expected_behavior: Restrict every retained evaluation-seed classification to exactly one of anchor_candidate, challenge_candidate, or non_baseline_exploratory_candidate.
forbidden_result: A seed uses a classification outside the closed permitted set.
A seed is promoted through an unapproved or baseline classification.
obligations.observable_result: Each retained seed record has a classification from the closed permitted set and rejects any other value.
obligations.state_after: All retained seeds use only the permitted non-baseline classification set.
obligations.state_before: Seed records may state an approved non-baseline classification without closed-set validation.
obligations.subject: Evaluation-seed classification
obligations.trigger: A retained seed record is validated.

obligations.expected_behavior: Require every Matrix Case to own a distinct fixture or state transition in addition to distinct inputs and separated Stable and Candidate state.
forbidden_result: A Matrix Case reuses another case's fixture or state transition.
Distinct labels or hashes alone establish case distinction.
obligations.observable_result: Each of the six Matrix Cases is bound to its own fixture or state transition and reuse is rejected.
obligations.state_after: All Matrix Cases have independently owned fixtures or state transitions.
obligations.state_before: Matrix Cases have distinctness claims without verified per-case fixture or state-transition ownership.
obligations.subject: Matrix Case fixture or state-transition ownership
obligations.trigger: The replay Matrix is assembled or verified.

obligations.expected_behavior: Demonstrate preserved behavior for every Matrix Case that is unaffected by the Candidate change.
forbidden_result: An unaffected case lacks a preserved-behavior observation.
Unrelated behavior is treated as preserved without case-specific execution evidence.
obligations.observable_result: Each unaffected Matrix Case has an attributable observation showing its required behavior remains preserved.
obligations.state_after: Preserved behavior is established for all unaffected Matrix Cases.
obligations.state_before: Unchanged Matrix Cases have no independent preserved-behavior obligation or observation.
obligations.subject: Unaffected Matrix Cases

obligations.expected_behavior: Invalidate the Matrix aggregate whenever an expected output or expectation is forged.
forbidden_result: Forged expected output is accepted as case evidence.
A forged expectation allows the aggregate to succeed.
obligations.observable_result: Tampered expected output or expectation deterministically causes aggregate invalidation.
obligations.state_after: The aggregate is rejected when any expected output or expectation is forged.
obligations.state_before: Expected-difference constraints exist, but general expectation forgery is not independently rejected.
obligations.subject: Expectation-forged Matrix evidence
obligations.trigger: Matrix expectations or expected outputs are checked.

obligations.expected_behavior: Prevent a success path from making any required Consumer route check unreachable.
forbidden_result: A required Consumer route check is bypassed on a successful path.
Success is reported while required route checks cannot execute.
obligations.observable_result: Reachability validation proves every required Consumer route check remains executable on successful execution paths.
obligations.state_after: All required Consumer route checks are reachable on success paths.
obligations.state_before: Consumer closure and invocation bindings do not independently establish success-path reachability.
obligations.subject: Required Consumer route checks

obligations.expected_behavior: During re-enable, invoke the current approved Candidate Route through the Consumer and capture its current result.
forbidden_result: Re-enable uses a stale or unapproved Candidate Route.
Re-enable is reported without an actual Candidate invocation or current-result capture.
obligations.observable_result: A re-enable receipt binds the current approved Candidate identity, actual invocation, and captured current result.
obligations.state_after: Re-enable has executed the current approved Candidate Route and recorded its result.
obligations.state_before: Re-enable execution is not independently bound to current approval, Candidate identity, and result capture.
obligations.subject: Re-enable transition
obligations.trigger: A Candidate Route is re-enabled after disable or rollback.

obligations.expected_behavior: Preserve failed-Candidate evidence while adding new Consumer and rollback evidence append-only.
forbidden_result: Failed-Candidate evidence is deleted, rewritten, or replaced by later Consumer or rollback evidence.
New evidence overwrites historical failed-Candidate records.
obligations.observable_result: Failed-Candidate records remain intact and subsequent Consumer and rollback records are appended under isolated evidence boundaries.
obligations.state_after: Failed-Candidate evidence is preserved and new Consumer/rollback evidence is append-only.
obligations.state_before: Historical preservation and append-only repair are specified, but failed-Candidate evidence preservation is not independently bound.
obligations.subject: Failed-Candidate evidence
obligations.trigger: Consumer or rollback evidence is recorded after a failed Candidate evaluation.

obligations.expected_behavior: Restrict terminal results to pass, comparison-failed, invalid-input, identity-invalid, evidence-invalid, stale, execution-failed, timed-out, or the permitted expected-difference case, and prevent serialized aliases from merging failures into success or silently reinterpreting a category.
forbidden_result: An undeclared terminal category is accepted.
A serialized alias converts a failure to success or silently changes category meaning.
obligations.observable_result: Terminal-category validation accepts only the declared set and rejects invalid or semantically reinterpreted aliases.
obligations.state_after: Terminal categories and alias semantics are validated against the declared contract.
obligations.state_before: Deterministic terminal states exist without an independent category-set and alias-preservation check.
obligations.subject: Terminal result categories
obligations.trigger: A replay or Matrix result is serialized or interpreted.

obligations.expected_behavior: Reject creation of another TC-D1 requirement tree.
forbidden_result: A replacement or additional TC-D1 requirement tree is created or accepted.
A new requirement tree is used to bypass the canonical package.
obligations.observable_result: An attempted additional TC-D1 requirement tree is deterministically rejected as out of scope.
obligations.state_after: Only the canonical TC-D1 requirement tree remains in scope.
obligations.state_before: Scope exclusions do not independently prohibit creation of another TC-D1 requirement tree.
obligations.subject: TC-D1 requirement-tree boundary
obligations.trigger: A TC-D1 requirement tree creation is proposed or attempted.

obligations.expected_behavior: Reject redesign of Skill-input v1/current-pointer semantics while retaining current Skill-input v2 behavior.
forbidden_result: Skill-input v1 or current-pointer semantics are redesigned under this scope.
Current Skill-input v2 behavior is replaced or weakened by the redesign.
obligations.observable_result: A proposed v1/current-pointer semantic redesign is rejected and the existing v2 contract remains the governed behavior.
obligations.state_after: Legacy v1/current-pointer semantics remain unchanged and Skill-input v2 remains in force.
obligations.state_before: Snapshot binding mentions v2 but does not independently enforce the v1/current-pointer redesign boundary.
obligations.subject: Skill-input semantic boundary
obligations.trigger: A Skill-input semantic change is proposed within TC-D1 work.

obligations.expected_behavior: Allow omission of a Consumer transition only when an existing authorized repository or ADR owner has approved and bound the exception; until that confirmation and binding exist, no exception exists.
forbidden_result: A Consumer transition is omitted without approval from an existing authorized repository or ADR owner.
An unbound or merely asserted exception is treated as valid.
The default is treated as exempt before confirmation.
obligations.observable_result: Each omitted transition has a pre-bound approval identifying an existing authorized repository or ADR owner; otherwise omission is rejected.
obligations.state_after: Consumer-transition omission is accepted only with the required authorized, bound exception.
obligations.state_before: Applicability exceptions require pre-execution binding but their approving authority and no-exception default are not independently enforced.
obligations.subject: Consumer Manifest exception authority
obligations.trigger: A Consumer transition omission or applicability exception is evaluated.
